t: Founded around 1465 by Kerei and Janibek, who broke away from the Uzbek ruler Abu'l-Khayr Khan with their followers.
A nomadic confederation of three juzes under Genghisid khans, with law kept by biys and codified in the Zhety Zhargy.
Dzungar invasions after 1723 drove the juzes towards Russia, which abolished the khans' power in the 1820s.
dyk: The name Kazakh is generally explained as meaning a free or independent wanderer, a word once used of men who had broken away from their own tribe or ruler.
ev: Kerei and Janibek lead their followers from the Uzbek Khanate into Moghulistan
Tauekel Khan takes Tashkent and Turkistan from Bukhara
Jahangir Khan checks the Dzungars at the Battle of Orbulaq
Tauke Khan's reign; the Zhety Zhargy law code is attributed to him
Dzungar invasion begins the 'Years of the Great Disaster'
Abulkhair Khan of the Junior Juz swears allegiance to Russia
Russia abolishes the khanship in the Middle Juz
Kenesary Kasymov, the last khan, is killed and his revolt ends

f.capital: Sygnak and other Syr Darya towns; later Turkistan
f.successor: Senior, Middle and Junior Juz; Russian Empire
